elements.title: Auditorium Building (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that US president Grover Cleveland declined to lay the cornerstone for the Auditorium Building (pictured) after laborers complained that he was not a union worker?

elements.title: The Fallen Crimson (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a song on Envy's album The Fallen Crimson features screaming over quiet music?

elements.title: Initial Deed (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Initial Deed was so named because the grantees were identified only by their initials?

elements.title: Merdeka Lions (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Merdeka Lions were initially created for a bridge before ultimately being moved to a military institute?

elements.title: Please (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the album Please by Sondre Lerche focuses on a breakup, but was nonetheless described as containing "a manic joy to the whole affair where one might expect sober reflection"?

elements.title: a Lego set (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a journalist sent copies of a Lego set to several major architecture firms to see what they would create with it?

elements.title: Jo Myong Ae (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that North Korean dancer Jo Myong Ae gained a fanbase of more than 17,000 people in South Korea?

elements.title: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction, first published in 1979, won Hugo Awards both as a printed book and as an online encyclopedia?

elements.title: Samuel Leve (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Samuel Leve's lighting design for Marilyn Monroe's famous 1962 performance of "Happy Birthday, Mr. President" unintentionally made her dress become see-through?
